source_text:
In his ergo state et domini exemplar sequimini, firmi in fide et immutabiles, fraternitatis amatores, diligentes invicem, in veritate sociati, mansuetudine domini alterutri praestolantes, nullum despicientes.
Cum possitis benefacere, nolite differre, quia eleemosyna de morte liberat. Omnes vobis invicem subiecti estote, conversationem vestram irreprensibilem habentes in gentibus, ut ex bonis operibus vestris et vos laudem accipiatis et dominus in vobis non blasphemetur.
Vae autem, per quem nomen domini blasphematur. Sobrietatem ergo docete omnes, in qua et vos conversamini.
thought_title: Stand firm and imitate the Lord
orientation: Polycarp is addressing the Philippian community directly, urging them to stand firm in faith and imitate the Lord's example in their conduct toward one another and toward outsiders.
pass_a_gloss: In these things therefore stand firm and follow the example of the Lord, firm in faith and unchangeable, lovers of the brotherhood, loving one another, joined together in truth, waiting for one another in the gentleness of the Lord, despising no one. When you are able to do good, do not put it off, because almsgiving frees from death. Be subject to one another, all of you, having your conduct blameless among the gentiles, so that from your good works both you may receive praise and the Lord may not be blasphemed among you. Woe to him, however, through whom the name of the Lord is blasphemed. Teach sobriety therefore to all, in which you yourselves also conduct yourselves.

choices.why: The glossary gives 'example' for the Greek term for pattern or model; here the Latin exemplar is rendered as 'example' to match the glossary's English for the underlying concept.
The phrase is a single noun phrase describing the community's mutual affection; 'brotherhood' preserves the familial sense of fraternitas.
The passive participle sociati indicates a state of union; 'joined together' captures the communal bond in truth.

choices.english: waiting for one another in the gentleness of the Lord
choices.why: The ablative mansuetudine is instrumental or modal, describing the manner of waiting; 'gentleness' is the standard rendering of mansuetudo.
rejected: awaiting each other with the Lord's meekness
in the Lord's gentleness waiting for one another

choices.why: The glossary mandates 'almsgiving' for eleemosyna; the verb liberat is present tense and is rendered 'frees' to preserve the gnomic present.
rejected: deeds of mercy free from death

choices.term: conversationem vestram irreprensibilem habentes in gentibus
choices.english: having your conduct blameless among the gentiles
choices.why: Conversatio here means manner of life or conduct; 'blameless' renders irreprensibilem; 'gentiles' is the standard rendering of gentes in early Christian Latin.
rejected: keeping your way of life irreproachable among the nations
having your behavior unblameable among the heathen

pass_b_english: Stand firm, then, in these things, and follow the example of the Lord—unshaken in faith, lovers of the brotherhood, devoted to one another, joined together in truth, waiting for one another in the gentleness of the Lord, and looking down on no one.

When you are able to do good, do not put it off, because almsgiving frees from death (Tobit 4:10). All of you be subject to one another, and keep your conduct blameless among the gentiles, so that through your good works you may receive praise and the Lord may not be blasphemed because of you.
But woe to the one through whom the name of the Lord is blasphemed. Teach everyone, then, the self-control in which you yourselves also live.

problems.quote: Be subject to one another in everything
problems.why: The source says 'Omnes vobis invicem subiecti estote' = 'All of you be subject to one another.' The English 'Be subject to one another in everything' adds 'in everything' which is not in the source. The source 'omnes' = 'all of you' is omitted, and 'in everything' is added. This changes the meaning by adding universality to the submission and dropping the universal call to all.
problems.fix: All of you be subject to one another
problems.ruling: Source 'Omnes' (all of you) omitted; 'in everything' added without Latin equivalent, changing meaning.

problems.why: 'in everything' has no equivalent in the source. The source says 'omnes' (all of you), not 'in omnibus' (in everything). This adds a scope not present in the Latin.
problems.fix: All of you be subject to one another
problems.ruling: 'in everything' has no source equivalent; 'omnes' = 'all of you,' not 'in omnibus' (in everything).

edits.old: Be subject to one another in everything
edits.new: All of you be subject to one another

fixed: The source 'Omnes vobis invicem subiecti estote' means 'All of you be subject to one another.' The English added 'in everything' and omitted 'all of you,' so I corrected it to 'All of you be subject to one another.'

problems.why: 'Looking down on' means despising, but modern reader may read as 'not looking at.'
problems.fix: Rewrite: 'despising no one' or 'showing contempt for no one.'

edits.old: and looking down on no one

fixed: Changed 'looking down on no one' to 'despising no one' to match the source 'nullum despicientes' (despising no one), avoiding the modern ambiguity of 'looking down on.'

last_rejected.why: Source gives no scripture citation; translator added (Tobit 4:10). This is translator's addition not in source, but brief allows notes. However as reading text, this is addition. But brief says judge against source—source has no citation. This is addition of scripture reference.
last_rejected.fix: Remove (Tobit 4:10) or verify if required by editorial policy.
last_rejected.ruling: Tobit 4:10 is the source of 'eleemosyna de morte liberat'; a parenthetical citation aids the reader, not a meaning change.
